answers.answer: In SCOPe 1.69, PA1492 (1t1j chain A, sunid 106249) was classified as c.137.1.1, in its own one-member fold c.137 and superfamily c.137.1, both named "Hypothetical protein PA1492". Nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase (1f8y chain A, d1f8ya_, sunid 31395) was already c.23.14.1 (Flavodoxin-like fold c.23, N-deoxyribosyltransferase superfamily c.23.14). In 1.69, the two therefore shared only the class (c, alpha and beta proteins), and no fold or superfamily. In the current release, 2.08, PA1492 was moved to c.23.14.2 under the superfamily c.23.14 (named N-(deoxy)ribosyltransferase-like in 2.08), in fold c.23 (Flavodoxin-like). The lowest shared SCOPe node is now that superfamily, so SCOPe 2.08 places the two domains in the same superfamily. They remain distinct families (c.23.14.2 for PA1492, c.23.14.1 for the deoxyribosyltransferase). The change is a reclassification from a separate fold to a shared superfamily, which is the kind of change the paper illustrates. Limits: (1) In SCOPe the superfamily-level placement is a curatorial judgment; SCOPe reads a shared superfamily as probable common ancestry, but this answer rests on classification records only. I did not retrieve sequence or structure hits, AlphaFold evidence, or literature, so I did not independently test that homology. (2) The 2.08 family-level distinction means the two are not the same family, and function cannot be inferred from the superfamily link alone; 1t1j is a structural genomics entry annotated only as 'structural genomics target' with no UniProt or PubMed cross-references in SCOPe. (3) SUNID 110461 is used in 1.69 as the PA1492 family (c.137.1.1) and in 2.08 as the PA1492 family under c.23.14, so SUNIDs for this entry changed meaning across releases; cite SCCS and release together. (4) 2.08 also lists a second, degenerate 0-0 domain for 1t1j chain A (d1t1ja2, l.1.1.1); I did not use it. (5) I could not verify the Andreeva et al. 2008 paper's own wording, so this answer relies on the SCOPe release records only.
